name: CardiacLens v9.10.347.206
notes: Secure Access: fixed the intermittent mis-tap bug where tapping one key could register a different key elsewhere on the grid. Root cause: two full, competing lock-screen implementations were both live and both wired to the same lock button, sharing the same stored key/color. The newer 'Takeover' system silently overwrote the older, complete system's tap/unlock functions on three separate delayed timers (100ms/1s/4s after load), while the older system's on-screen keyboard buttons were still calling those functions by reference. Takeover has been permanently disabled (code retained but never invoked; nothing outside its own block referenced it, confirmed by search). The original system is now the sole implementation.

Secure Access: separately, closed a real race condition in the original system itself. After a wrong 4-tap sequence, the keyboard fully rebuilds with a new randomized layout 450ms later. A tap already in progress when that rebuild happened could land on whatever key ended up at the same screen position in the new layout. The grid is now locked to input the instant a wrong sequence completes, and unlocked again the instant the new grid renders, closing the gap entirely.

Fluid reminders: real background push notifications (the kind that arrive when the app is closed or the phone is locked) were not carrying any identifying information to the tap handler at all -- sw.js's push handler built the visible notification but never attached the underlying data payload to it, so tapping had nothing to route on. Now fixed: the tag survives to tap time, and any fluid-reminder notification (pacing, or any fluid push where no specific event applies) opens Log Fluid directly instead of falling back to the generic Events screen.
label: SecureAccessConsolidationAndFluidTapRouting
summary: Consolidated Secure Access to a single lock-screen implementation and closed the tap-registration race condition behind the intermittent 'wrong key selected' bug. Fixed real background fluid push notifications so they reliably open Log Fluid.
fixes: Secure Access: disabled the duplicate 'Takeover' lock-screen system that was silently overwriting the working system's tap handlers on a delay.
Secure Access: grid now locks to input immediately on a failed sequence and unlocks immediately when the new grid renders, closing the async rebuild race.
Fluid push notifications: sw.js now attaches notification data so tap routing has something to work with; fluid-reminder taps route straight to Log Fluid.
testing: node --check passed on sw.js and all 7 inline <script> blocks in index.html.

Extracted the actual shipped Secure Access functions (not a reconstruction) and ran them under Node with hand-built DOM/localStorage stubs: confirmed the grid locks to pointer input the instant a wrong 4-tap sequence completes, confirmed it unlocks again the instant the rebuilt grid renders, and confirmed a correct M/purple/purple/purple sequence still unlocks normally both before and after a rebuild.

First version of the pointer-events fix set the lock but never released it after rebuild, since innerHTML replaces the container's children, not the container itself, which would have permanently frozen the keyboard after any single wrong sequence. Caught by the test above before release, not after. Fixed by explicitly clearing pointerEvents at the start of _clRenderKeyboard.

R18 (mandatory runtime execution test): loaded the actual full index.html in real headless Chromium (pre-installed at /opt/pw-browsers, referenced by this app's own release checklist) with realistic localStorage (disclaimer accepted, BP_TRACKER_<today> with 2 readings, Can's real Secure Access profile: letter M, color purple). Zero uncaught page errors across the full load and interaction sequence. Confirmed in the real browser, not a stub: window._clKeyTap is still the original system's function (Takeover never overwrote it); window.CardiacLensSecureTakeover was never created (boot() never ran); opened the real lock screen, and tapped the actual 30 rendered .cl-kb-key buttons via real click() in the correct M/purple/purple/purple sequence -- the app genuinely unlocked. Confirmed _clOpenEventFromTag('cardiaclens-fluid-reminder') calls the real logFluid() in the real page context. Console showed only expected network failures (403s and CORS blocks fetching cardiaclens.com and worker endpoints from a local file:// origin with no network access) -- none produced an uncaught page error.

Prior to the real-browser test above, the same functions were also verified in isolation: extracted the actual shipped Secure Access, Takeover, and notification-routing code and ran it under Node with hand-built DOM/localStorage stubs. This caught a real bug in the first version of the pointer-events fix (it locked the keyboard but never released it after rebuild, which would have permanently frozen input after any single wrong sequence) before it went any further. Fixed and re-verified.

Not tested: an actual physical tap on a real iPhone touchscreen, and an actual real push notification delivered through the live Cloudflare Worker (both require genuine hardware/network this environment cannot simulate). Everything else -- syntax, logic, and full-page runtime behavior including real DOM clicks -- was verified against the real shipped code, not a description of it.
